contracts.semantic_clause:
### Dedicated migration distribution contract

The sole special use of OOP Git ancestry is optional technical migration discovery through dist/migrations/index.json. Ordinary interaction, context assembly, bootstrap and producer validation MUST NOT require an OOP history walk, previous object, diff or ancestry proof. Current repository/ref/full commit identity remains available metadata under BOOT-04, not release certification. Organizational decision/event history, source control and authorized publication retain their existing rules.

Every adoptable distribution MUST contain a versioned, source-bound, reviewed index with an explicit not_required, required or unknown disposition for each of common, runtime and operations. Absence or incomplete facts never implies no-op. Required scope descriptors MUST declare stable migration/requirement identities, ownership, affected domains, dependencies/order, applicability, source/target semantics, authority, pre/postconditions, already-satisfied detection, verification and resumable partial-effect recovery. Paths are exact safe package-relative references; future containing commit identities MUST NOT be embedded as self-references. Source governance remains authoritative; consumer interpretation is not producer hash/schema auditing.

Current compatibility.json MUST retain the requirements for every explicitly supported prior state schema/fingerprint, including actual-state predicates, read/write compatibility, preservation/grandfathering policy and necessary recovery. Stable reviewed intent identities survive amend/rebase; neither SHA order nor one increasing global counter establishes compatibility. Unknown/unsupported profiles, incomplete descriptors, changed authority, conflicting evidence and unknown partial effects block only dependent unsafe work with an observable next action. No mandatory service, fixed physical private layout or vendor adapter is introduced.

The supported-state catalog MUST be cumulative and governed by explicit version-independent reviewed decisions: retain every still-supported profile, its state schemas, scope predicates, read/write compatibility, preconditions, ordered requirements, transformations, already-satisfied tests and recovery. The immediate prior/current identity pair, generation, publication, amend or absent Git objects MUST NOT silently remove support. Each withdrawal MUST identify affected stable identities, reason, risk, compatibility impact, authorized disposition, attributable evidence and safe scoped recovery; it never declares affected deployed consumers updated.

A legacy runtime may retain only its full adopted OOP SHA and inspectable actual state, without a source fingerprint or reachable old object. Identify a supported state shape from available authenticated project/root/runtime ownership, observed schemas and record shapes, stable requirement/effect evidence or an independently trusted existing mapping; a SHA or arbitrary profile label alone is insufficient. Multiple materially conflicting profiles, missing observations, incompatible writes or unknown partial effects remain UNKNOWN/BLOCKED with scoped recovery and no verified checkpoint advancement. Content-equivalent profiles may share verified semantics without inventing transformations. Current declarations cannot alone prove that a rewritten catalog preserved all prior decisions: qualify longitudinal claims against independently attributable accepted support evidence when available, otherwise record NOT VERIFIED without requiring old commits or a mandatory registry. Read this migration context only on applicable update/migration triggers; consumers never run producer tests, hash packages or certify releases.

If a complete eligible published path is safely determined, inspect each subsequent publication on the canonical first-parent line in order, excluding the prior adopted commit. For ABC → DEF → GHI → LMN → OPQ and verified DEF, inspect GHI, LMN, OPQ. Unincorporated branch commits are not adoption epochs; a merge descriptor covers net introduced requirements. Inspect old distributions through isolated reads, never mutate a dirty primary checkout. If ancestry is unavailable, shallow, rewritten, divergent or the prior object disappeared, use the current supported-state contract instead. A metadata-only amend may reuse equivalent current facts/evidence and adopt its new full identity without inventing a migration; SHA equality or difference alone does not establish equivalence.

Reconcile three independently owned destinations at each relevant step. Common is only the authorized actually shared project-private root; another machine's separate root is not updated. Use existing atomic/conflict-safe private writes and preserve unrelated data/secrets. Runtime is the active instance's private adapters, knowledge/context and checkpoint; peers never advance it. Operations is the one canonical project organizational source or its authoritative references; inspect its records and actual effects, independently gate reads/writes, reuse verified shared work and never downgrade an advanced state to an intermediate publication label. Replay-sensitive common actions retain explicit runtime ownership within the existing shared-private authority boundary; organization actions belong to operations.

For each applicable destination record UPDATE_APPLIED_VERIFIED, ALREADY_SATISFIED, NOT_REQUIRED, PENDING, BLOCKED or UNKNOWN with scope, identity, observations, evidence and next action. Already satisfied requires current attributable actual facts and stable requirement evidence, not a private flag, peer checkpoint, model assertion, hash or command success. Apply only unsatisfied owned actions. After all applicable compatibility/migration, activation, adapter and context gates pass, atomically advance only this runtime's full verified_commit and repository/ref/evidence; retain prior verification and a separate pending/failed attempt otherwise. Preserved adoption does not imply rollback of partial organizational effects.

An organizationally relevant, previously unrecorded alignment can require canonical communication even at a no-transformation GHI or OPQ step. Its descriptor MUST distinguish organizational_state_change from an alignment attestation, causally bind scope and stable semantic requirements, and state when publication is needed. Reuse equivalent sufficient canonical evidence; do not append a record for every runtime or rewritten SHA, overwrite advanced facts, or invent data transformation. When required evidence is absent, perform the existing authorized signed operations Git commit/push with expected-ref conflict control and canonical remote readback. Local commit, isolated branch, lockfile or failed push is not remote synchronization or exclusive authority over external effects. A losing claimant rereads canonical revision and actual effects before safe continuation; never blindly replay.

Split effects into scoped resumable actions under existing organizational migration policy. Reconcile actual facts after interruption/timeout before retry, keep pending/failed facts distinct and preserve current successful scoped evidence. Unknown required remote readback keeps organizational publication pending; offline remote identity/freshness stays unknown. An older joining runtime may retain read compatibility while writes remain blocked. Independent informational G0 work continues when safe; project switching invalidates project context and authority. This contract never updates another runtime's private state or claims installed interoperability from structural/synthetic checks.


RUNTIME-08 — The current supported-state migration distribution MUST cover reconciliation of legacy per-session adoption under RUNTIME-06. Common scope reconciles the authoritative runtime mapping/supersession when applicable; runtime scope reconciles owned checkpoints, adapters and session evidence readers. An already correct mapping is verified and reused. Retain prior supported profiles, sufficient evidence and existing valid administrative receipts; do not automatically promote old labels. This technical ownership reconciliation alone requires no canonical business-data transformation or per-session organizational publication. Independently applicable organizational alignment/publication and authority requirements remain binding.
